NDT training in Edmonton: how it works for Edmonton employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET for Edmonton employers and technicians, live online or onsite at your own facility, under ASNT Level III oversight. There is no Atlantis classroom in Edmonton. The training suits companies that certify staff to an SNT-TC-1A written practice, usually because they work to US codes or for US clients. It is not CAN/CGSB-48.9712 (CGSB) certification, which is Canada's national scheme.

That last point matters more in Edmonton than almost anywhere else in North America, so it is worth being plain about it up front. Canada has a national, third-party NDT personnel certification scheme: CAN/CGSB-48.9712, the Canadian adoption of ISO 9712. Natural Resources Canada's National NDT Certification Body (NDTCB) certifies individuals to it, and the CWB Group is also authorized to certify NDT personnel. When the Canadian General Standards Board wound down its operations in 2026, NRCan confirmed that the NDTCB and existing certifications carry on without interruption, so the scheme is unchanged for technicians. Many Alberta owners, and much provincially regulated pressure-equipment work, expect that CGSB-style certificate. CGSB training has to come from an NRCan Recognized Training Organization, and Atlantis does not claim that status. Our courses do not count toward CGSB training requirements.

Where does SNT-TC-1A training fit, then? It fits the part of the Edmonton market that answers to American paperwork. That includes Nisku and Leduc module yards building to ASME Section VIII or ASME B31.3 for US-stamped or US-owned projects, and inspection companies whose parent or main client works under an SNT-TC-1A written practice. It also covers contractors sending crews south of the border on rotation, pipeline service firms supporting cross-border systems, and manufacturers whose US customers audit to ASNT-based procedures. For those employers the certificate that counts is the one their own written practice produces, and Atlantis can supply the training, the examinations and the Level III oversight behind it. For employers who need both, the practical approach is dual qualification: CGSB for the Canadian owner and SNT-TC-1A for the US client. We help with the SNT-TC-1A side and with the written practice that keeps the two apart.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Edmonton

Every course follows the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge for its method and level. Theory can be delivered live online. The hands-on part runs on your equipment and specimens at your site, or on specimens we arrange for an onsite cohort. How many hours each level needs is set by your written practice, using SNT-TC-1A's recommended guidelines as the baseline. The NDT training requirements matrix sets them out method by method, and we don't repeat the figures here because your written practice may set different ones.

MethodLevelsWhat Edmonton employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic testing)I, II, IIIThickness surveys on Industrial Heartland piping and vessels, weld inspection on module and spool fabrication, lamination checks on plateLevel I: none beyond employer entry rules. Level II: Level I plus documented experience
PAUT (phased array)II, IIIWeld volumetric inspection on process piping and pipeline girth welds where RT is being replaced, corrosion mappingUT Level II is normally expected first
TOFD (time-of-flight diffraction)II, IIIHeavy-wall vessel seam welds, flaw sizing alongside PAUT on fabrication and in-service workUT Level II is normally expected first
RT (radiographic testing)I, II, IIIWeld radiography on piping spools and pipeline tie-ins, film and digital interpretationRadiation safety qualification is separate. See the CNSC note below
MT (magnetic particle)I, II, IIISurface-crack checks on structural steel, lifting gear, rotating equipment and fabricated weldsNone beyond employer entry rules
PT (liquid penetrant)I, II, IIIStainless and non-magnetic welds, machined parts, valve and pump componentsNone beyond employer entry rules
VT (visual testing)I, II, IIIWeld and fit-up visual inspection, in-service visual of tanks, vessels and structuresNone beyond employer entry rules
ET (eddy current)I, II, IIIHeat-exchanger and condenser tube inspection during plant shutdowns, surface-crack detection on conductive partsNone beyond employer entry rules

Ultrasonic testing. UT Level I teaches sound physics, couplants, straight-beam thickness gauging and instrument calibration on reference blocks. Level II adds angle-beam weld inspection, distance-amplitude correction, flaw characterisation, and evaluating results against an acceptance standard such as ASME Section VIII or ASME B31.3. In Edmonton the everyday UT jobs are corrosion surveys on ageing process units and weld inspection in the fabrication shops south of the city. Most of the second group is thick-wall carbon steel, so beam-path geometry and skip distances get extra practice time.

PAUT and TOFD. These advanced UT methods are taught at Level II and III on top of a UT Level II foundation. Coursework covers focal laws, sectorial and linear scans, encoded scanning, and setup files. For TOFD it adds lateral-wave and back-wall interpretation and the method's near-surface dead zone. Edmonton demand comes from two directions: fabricators replacing radiography on spool and module welds to keep bays free of exclusion zones, and in-service teams mapping corrosion and sizing cracks during turnarounds.

Radiographic testing. RT courses cover source and X-ray tube principles, film and digital detector techniques, image quality indicators, exposure calculation and weld interpretation. Canadian radiation safety is a separate legal requirement, covered in the FAQ below. Our RT training teaches the NDT method. It does not qualify anyone to operate an exposure device in Canada.

MT, PT and VT. These are the entry points for most new technicians and still earn their keep on every Edmonton shutdown. MT covers yoke, prod and coil techniques, wet and dry particles, fluorescent inspection and demagnetisation. PT covers penetrant families, dwell times, removal methods and developer choice. VT covers weld profile, undercut, porosity, gauges and the visual acceptance criteria written into the governing code.

Eddy current. ET covers impedance-plane analysis, probe selection, calibration standards and tube inspection techniques. Heat exchangers and condensers are the main reason an Edmonton employer asks for ET. The course can be tuned to the tube materials and bundle types your crew will actually see.

Level III. Candidates preparing for the ASNT NDT Level III exams (Basic plus method examinations) can use our ASNT Level III exam preparation. For many Edmonton companies, though, the more urgent need is a Level III to run their SNT-TC-1A programme, which is covered further down.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Edmonton, step by step

SNT-TC-1A certification is employer-based. Your employer certifies you against its own written practice, and nobody in Edmonton or Ottawa issues the certificate. Most US-facing employers follow the same sequence:

  1. The employer adopts a written practice. This is the controlling document. It defines levels, training hours, experience, examinations, vision requirements and who may certify. With no written practice, SNT-TC-1A certification does not exist. See written practice development.
  2. Classroom training. The candidate completes the formal training hours the written practice requires for the method and level, online, onsite or both. Hours for each method and level are in the training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. The candidate logs supervised experience in the method, in the hours and form the written practice sets. In Edmonton it usually builds up on fabrication-shop work and shutdown campaigns, and the log must be signed and traceable.
  4. General examination. A written test of method theory and principles.
  5. Specific examination. A written test on the employer's procedures, equipment and the codes and specifications the technician will work to, for example ASME B31.3 acceptance criteria for a piping fabricator.
  6. Practical examination. Hands-on testing of real specimens with known discontinuities, graded against a checklist. A Level III, or a person the Level III designates under the written practice, administers and grades the examinations.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast checks, and near vision is repeated annually.
  8. Certification. The employer's certifying authority signs the certification, and the record goes into the employee's file.
  9. Recertification. Certifications lapse at the interval set in the written practice. Recertification is by re-examination or by the evidence of continuing satisfactory work the written practice allows. When a technician changes employer, the new employer has to certify them again under its own written practice.

For the full SNT-TC-1A picture, including how it differs from central schemes such as CGSB, see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Edmonton crews

Atlantis has no training centre in Edmonton, so every programme uses one of three delivery models.

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led virtual sessions for general and method theory, working through the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge, with quizzes and mock exams. Edmonton is on Mountain Time, and sessions can be scheduled to suit shift patterns. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility. An instructor comes to your shop, yard or plant and runs hands-on sessions and practical examinations on your own instruments, probes and specimens. This works well for Nisku and Leduc fabricators and for inspection companies with a shop and a crew available at the same time. See corporate NDT training.
  • Blended. Theory is done online over a few weeks, and a short onsite block covers the practical and the exams.

The Edmonton calendar revolves around plant turnarounds. The Industrial Heartland and the refineries run large planned shutdowns, and in the months before one every inspection company tries to get technicians qualified and every trainer is booked. The best time to train is before the turnaround pre-planning window, when crews are available and there's still time to finish on-the-job hours. Tell us your shutdown dates and we will schedule theory to finish in time for practical exams before mobilisation. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day. Request an Edmonton training quote.

Where NDT technicians work in Edmonton

Edmonton's NDT work is spread across a few distinct clusters, and each asks for a slightly different mix of methods and paperwork.

  • Alberta's Industrial Heartland. Northeast of the city through Strathcona County, Fort Saskatchewan and Sturgeon County is a dense belt of refining, upgrading, petrochemical, fertilizer and chemical plants. In-service inspection there means UT thickness, PAUT corrosion mapping, RT and ET during turnarounds, and constant MT, PT and VT on repairs.
  • Pipeline terminals and midstream. The Edmonton area is a starting point for major export pipelines, including the Trans Mountain system to the west coast, and a hub for tank terminals, gas processing and NGL fractionation. Girth-weld inspection is done to CSA Z662, Canada's oil and gas pipeline systems standard. Interprovincial lines are regulated by the Canada Energy Regulator and provincial lines by the Alberta Energy Regulator.
  • Fabrication and module yards. Nisku, Leduc and the south-side industrial parks build pressure vessels, piping spools, skids and modules for Alberta and for export. Weld inspection there is volume work in UT, PAUT, RT, MT and PT. Much of the export work is built to ASME codes for US owners, which is exactly where SNT-TC-1A written practices are common.
  • Aviation and transport. Edmonton International Airport and the regional aviation and helicopter operators support maintenance work that uses ET, PT, MT and UT under Transport Canada rules and operator programmes. Rail and heavy-equipment repair shops add MT and UT on axles, frames and components.
  • Power and utilities. Thermal and cogeneration plants around the region need boiler tube, piping and turbine inspection during outages.

Codes and regulators Edmonton technicians run into. Pressure equipment in Alberta is regulated under the Safety Codes Act, with ABSA as the delegated pressure-equipment safety authority. Its requirements, and the owner's own quality programme, decide which NDT certification is acceptable for that work. CSA B51 covers boilers, pressure vessels and pressure piping in Canada, and it points to ASME for design and construction. ASME Section V (NDE methods), Section VIII (vessels) and B31.3 (process piping) show up on almost every Edmonton job pack. CSA Z662 covers pipelines, and CSA W59 and AWS D1.1 cover structural welding. Owner specifications at the big plants often go further than the codes.

What Edmonton employers typically ask for. Check job postings and you'll see the same pattern: CGSB certification in one or more methods for Canadian owner work, a CNSC Certified Exposure Device Operator for gamma radiography crews, and sometimes an SNT-TC-1A certification or US experience for contractors serving US clients. Driver's licences, H2S Alive and site-specific safety tickets are common extras. Figures for pay vary too much to quote responsibly. See the NDT salary guide for how level and method affect earnings.

Level III services and written practices for Edmonton NDT companies

This is where Atlantis is most useful to Edmonton companies. Any employer certifying staff under SNT-TC-1A needs a compliant written practice and access to a Level III who can write procedures, administer and grade examinations, and sign off on the programme. Many Alberta firms only need that capability for part of their book, typically when a US client, a US-stamped fabrication job or a cross-border contract asks for an SNT-TC-1A programme. Keeping a full-time Level III for that one requirement rarely makes sense.

  • Written practice development and review. We write an SNT-TC-1A written practice around your methods, levels and client requirements, or audit an existing one before a client audit. Where you also maintain CGSB-certified staff, the written practice can state clearly how the two schemes sit side by side. See written practice development.
  • Outsourced Level III. Procedure writing and review, technique sheets, examination creation and grading, review of practical examinations, and audit support.
  • Procedure alignment to code. We tie NDT procedures to the ASME, AWS or client specification that governs a given job, so that acceptance criteria, calibration and reporting all line up.
  • Corporate programmes. Structured Level I to II progression for new hires, and refreshers before a busy season. See corporate NDT training.

For the rules behind all of this, read SNT-TC-1A training and certification. Book a Level III consultation for your Edmonton company.

Practise before the practical exam

Most candidates find the practical examination the hardest part: finding and sizing real discontinuities in a set time, on specimens they haven't seen before. Atlantis trainees can practise with Practical NDT, a 3D simulator covering 12 NDT methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Edmonton trainees the oil and gas site and welding workshop scenes are the closest match to daily work. Use it to rehearse scan patterns, setup routines and interpretation between onsite sessions. It is a practice tool only. It does not replace hands-on training or the practical examination on real specimens that your written practice requires. For written exams, mock questions such as UT Level 2 practice questions help candidates find weak spots early.

Your instructor

Atlantis training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He oversees course content, examinations and written-practice work for every programme, including onsite cohorts for Edmonton employers.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Edmonton

How do I get NDT certified in Edmonton?

First decide which certificate you need. For most Canadian owner and provincially regulated work, that means CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification through the NRCan NDT Certification Body, with training from an NRCan Recognized Training Organization. If you are hired by, or already work for, an employer that certifies under an SNT-TC-1A written practice, your employer certifies you after training, experience, examinations and a vision test, and Atlantis can deliver the training and Level III examinations for that route.

Can I take NDT training online in Alberta?

Yes, for theory. General and method theory under SNT-TC-1A can be taught live online, and Atlantis does that for Alberta candidates. Hands-on training and the practical examination have to be done on real equipment and specimens, which we run onsite at the employer's facility. See online NDT training.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Edmonton employers?

It depends on the employer and the work. SNT-TC-1A certification belongs to the employer who issued it and is recognised within that employer's programme. Edmonton companies working to US codes or for US clients often use it. Many Canadian owners and provincially regulated pressure-equipment scopes expect CGSB certification instead. Always check the owner's specification and the employer's written practice.

Does Atlantis training count toward CGSB certification?

No, and we don't claim that it does. NRCan requires CGSB training from its Recognized Training Organizations, and Atlantis is not claiming that status. Our courses are for SNT-TC-1A programmes.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

That depends on the formal training and experience hours in your employer's written practice, and whether the candidate already holds UT Level I. SNT-TC-1A gives recommended minimums, and the training requirements matrix lists them. Experience hours usually take longer to build than classroom hours.

Do I need a licence for radiography in Alberta?

Gamma radiography with sealed sources is federally regulated by the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission. The company must hold a CNSC licence, and anyone operating an exposure device must be a CNSC Certified Exposure Device Operator or a trainee under the direct supervision and continuous observation of one. X-ray equipment is also subject to provincial radiation protection rules. Our RT course teaches the NDT method and does not grant any radiation licence or certification.

What does NDT training cost in Edmonton?

Pricing is quoted on request. It depends on the method, level, group size, whether delivery is online, onsite or blended, and whether Level III examination and written-practice work is included. Cohort and onsite quotes are turned around within one business day. Ask for a quote for your Edmonton crew.

Can you train our crew onsite in Nisku or Leduc?

Yes. Onsite training at your shop or yard is a core delivery model. We use your instruments and specimens where possible so the practical matches your procedures.

Which NDT method should a new technician start with?

Most Edmonton employers start new technicians on MT, PT and VT, then move them to UT, with PAUT and TOFD added once they reach UT Level II. RT comes with its own radiation safety track. Your employer's hiring plan should decide the order.

We need a Level III for a US client audit. Can Atlantis help?

Yes. Outsourced Level III services, written practice development and audit preparation are the core of what we offer Canadian companies with US-facing SNT-TC-1A programmes. See written practice development.

Can I prepare for the ASNT Level III exam from Edmonton?

Yes. Level III preparation is delivered live online. See ASNT Level III training.

What happens to my SNT-TC-1A certification if I change employers?

It doesn't transfer automatically. Your new employer has to certify you under its own written practice, though it can take your documented training and experience into account.
